domain: Public Health Ethics / Constitutional Law / Medical Autonomy
topic_summary: Analysis of vaccine mandate frameworks as a contested kernel where public-health-primary and bodily-autonomy-primary readings emit structurally different constraints with incompatible victim sets: the immunocompromised-exposed (public health reading) versus the unvaccinated-coerced (autonomy reading). Historical foundation in Jacobson v. Massachusetts (1905) establishes state police power; contemporary COVID-19 mandates for healthcare workers and large employers surface the kernel contest.

key_entities: Public Health Authorities (CDC, state health boards; mandate enforcement)
Immunocompromised Populations (vulnerable to severe disease; mandate beneficiaries under PH reading)
Mandate Opponents (healthcare workers, parents; coercion victims under autonomy reading)
U.S. Supreme Court (Jacobson precedent; constitutional arbiter)
key_tensions: Community protection vs individual autonomy (public health authority vs mandate opponents)
Vulnerable population safety vs healthcare worker consent (immunocompromised vs HCW autonomy)
Trust in institutions vs radicalization risk (mandate enforcement vs long-term public health legitimacy)

key_mechanisms.description: All 50 states require vaccination for public school entry; enforcement via exclusion
Population-level vaccination coverage protects those unable to vaccinate
key_mechanisms.targets: Immunocompromised, medically contraindicated, too young to vaccinate

key_mechanisms.description: OSHA workplace safety authority used to require vaccination or testing

key_absences.description: No structured compensation for vaccine injury under mandate (VICP exists but contested adequacy)
Mandates often lack genuine exit: homeschooling requires resources; job loss imposes severe costs

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The legitimate scope of state authority to compel medical intervention for collective benefit
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Constitutional police power (Jacobson precedent) interpreted through public health expertise vs individual rights frameworks

readings.commitment: State authority to compel vaccination is legitimate when necessary to protect vulnerable populations from serious harm
readings.authority_grounding: Jacobson precedent + epidemiological expertise + utilitarian harm prevention
readings.expected_structural_delta: Immunocompromised enter victim set when mandates absent; unvaccinated bear duty to protect; high ε from mandate absence

readings.commitment: Medical intervention without informed consent violates fundamental bodily integrity regardless of collective benefit
readings.authority_grounding: Nuremberg Code + liberal rights tradition + self-ownership principle
readings.expected_structural_delta: Unvaccinated-coerced enter victim set when mandates present; state becomes rights violator; high ε from mandate presence

readings.commitment: Mandate legitimacy depends on disease severity, vaccine safety/efficacy, and availability of less restrictive alternatives
readings.authority_grounding: Constitutional strict scrutiny + risk-benefit analysis + least restrictive means doctrine
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set conditional on disease parameters; measles mandate legitimate, flu mandate not; moderate ε varies by pathogen

axiom_contradictions.basis: Public health reading holds that collective harm prevention can override individual medical consent; autonomy reading holds that bodily integrity is categorically inviolable regardless of collective benefit. No single framework can hold both: accepting autonomy's axiom (consent is absolute) requires rejecting public health's axiom (consent is conditional on harm to others).

omegas.description: Does mandate enforcement radicalize hesitants, creating long-term trust erosion that reduces future vaccine uptake? If yes, public_health_primary reading's short-term protection may generate long-term vulnerability.
omegas.source: Deferred axis trust_erosion_feedback + research context on radicalization risk

omegas.description: Are exit options (homeschooling, job change) genuinely available across income strata? If not, bodily_autonomy_primary reading's coercion claim intensifies; mandate becomes Snare rather than Rope.

What disease severity/vaccine efficacy threshold makes proportionality_reading collapse into one of the primary readings? Measles (high severity, high efficacy) may collapse to public_health_primary; flu (low severity, moderate efficacy) may collapse to bodily_autonomy_primary.
Is VICP compensation adequate for vaccine injury under mandate? If not, public_health_primary reading imposes uncompensated harm on a subset, violating its own utilitarian logic.
omegas.source: Deferred axis compensation_mechanism_absence + research context on VICP contested adequacy

omegas.description: Has Jacobson precedent drifted from its original scope (local smallpox outbreak) to justify federal employer mandates for respiratory viruses? If yes, authority_grounding for public_health_primary reading may be weaker than claimed.
omegas.source: Commitment system drift_status=partial + historical vs contemporary mandate scope

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel contest confirmed: public_health_primary and bodily_autonomy_primary hold axioms that no single coherent framework can hold simultaneously (collective harm prevention overrides consent vs consent is categorically inviolable). Proportionality_reading attempts resolution via conditional framework but does not eliminate the axiom contradiction for edge cases (high-severity diseases vs low-severity diseases). Three readings selected capture the kernel topology.
